# [TASK] Spike: Vosk English/German model selection for accent robustness

## Task
Spike: evaluate Vosk model options for English and German for accent/dialect
robustness within the $0/offline constraint.

## Scope
Research and a documented decision — not the integration itself (that's Task
#212).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] English options compared (current small model vs. `vosk-model-en-us-0.22` or similar) against a quick accented-speech smoke test — compared against published WER benchmarks (LibriSpeech/TED-LIUM/call-center) instead of a live audio smoke test: this session has no network egress to the model-hosting domain, and #215 (the accented-recording fixture the smoke test would run against) doesn't exist yet. See ADR-021's Context section for the full reasoning.
- [x] German model options identified (e.g. `vosk-model-de-*`) and one selected — `vosk-model-small-de-0.15` chosen over `vosk-model-small-de-zamia-0.3`, `vosk-model-de-0.21`, and `vosk-model-de-tuda-0.6-900k`.
- [x] Download size and runtime RAM cost documented for each candidate (ai-service currently lazy-loads one model; two models held at once changes that cost) — comparison table in ADR-021; the ADR also flags that Task #212 must measure actual combined RSS rather than trust disk-size figures alone.
- [x] Decision and rationale written up (in the ADR from #198's Task #1 if it's a natural fit, or a short note in this Story — reviewer's call) before Task #2 starts — #198's ADR-020 covers an unrelated topic (NL query parsing), so this got its own ADR: `docs/architecture/adr/021-vosk-bilingual-model-selection.md`.

## Estimate
**Hours:** 4

## Notes
**Decision:** switch English from `vosk-model-small-en-us-0.15` to `vosk-model-en-us-0.22-lgraph` (128MB), and add `vosk-model-small-de-0.15` (45MB) as the first German model.

Full-size models (1.8GB to 4.4GB) are ruled out for both languages — they wouldn't fit ai-service's 768Mi memory / 512Mi ephemeral-storage limits even alone, let alone with a second language resident.

Comparison table, full reasoning, and the consequences for #212 are in ADR-021.
